request.deadline: 12 months from treasury withdrawal, with milestones through weeks 6, 12, 13, 16, 18, 24, 26, 39, and 52
deliverables: Constitute two advisory councils with charters, conflict-of-interest policies, named members, and meeting records.
Form a dOSPO legal entity as a United States 501(c)(3) public charity and publish governance documents.
Publish quarterly public outcome reports with Mill Law Firm financial review attached.
Run a dependency audit with SBOMs, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, and a coverage gap analysis.
Fund retainer cohorts for high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure using a published priority formula.
Launch a public CHAOSS-aligned health dashboard for funded projects.
Operate maintainer development, CodeForUs bounty, and ecosystem activation programs as described in the proposal.
request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting as Article II.7.5 administrator at withdrawal, with a target transition to a dOSPO 501(c)(3) subject to governance.
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano dOSPO and Open Maintenance Framework program to manage open source sustainability funds through four programs: Maintenance Fund, Maintainer Development, CodeForUs bounties, and Ecosystem Activation Reserve.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months to fund a Cardano dOSPO and OMF program.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 funds administrator at the moment of treasury withdrawal.
Mill Law Firm is designated as independent financial auditor on a quarterly cadence through Month 12.
The program will use four programs: a Maintenance Fund, Maintainer Development program, CodeForUs bounty program, and Ecosystem Activation Reserve.
The Maintenance Fund will deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months to support high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure selected by dependency centrality and bus factor data.
Before any WP2-WP5 disbursement, advisory council feedback will be published on-chain, while final allocation authority remains with the administrator.
The dOSPO legal entity is intended to be formed as a United States 501(c)(3) public charity by Month 6, with any administrator transition requiring DRep approval by on-chain Info Action.
The proposal targets 15 or more high-centrality projects funded by Month 12 and 40% of top-50 dependencies funded by Month 12.

The proposer says the OMF and dOSPO whitepapers were developed with experts from Bitergia, CHAOSS, Apache Software Foundation, Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust, Intersect, Andamio Platform, Modus Create, Leadingbit Solutions, and the Chinstrap Community.
The proposer cites websites, GitHub, OMF v1.0, and dOSPO v1.0 as verifiable history for his track record and proposal materials.

summary: The document describes a large one-year treasury request for an administrator-led open source sustainability program with advisory councils, financial review, dependency-based project selection, public reporting, and several governance-controlled accountability mechanisms, but some key credentials, partnerships, legal/audit arrangements, and external evidence are asserted rather than demonstrated in the anchor text.
